Friends
❓ How challenges work
  1. Challenge a player below: pick match play, stroke play or skins, the stake and the course. Your stake is held from when you send it; you get it back if they decline, you call it off, or nobody answers in 7 days.
  2. Once accepted, their stake is held too.
  3. You each play the 9 holes on your own PC, whenever you like (within 7 days). You don't play at the same time and you don't see each other's shots: the course, wind and greens are the same for both.
  4. When both cards are in, it settles by itself, handicap strokes included: the winner gets the pot and you both see the shared scorecard.
  5. Not played in time? Whoever didn't play forfeits; if neither did, both get their stake back.
  6. More than one friend? Host an invitational: invite as many as you like to stroke play or skins, start it once at least one has accepted, and the pot goes to the best net score.
You each play the round on your own PC · the bet settles when both cards are in
Challenge
How it works — you don't play at the same time, and you won't see each other's shots:
  1. Send it. Your stake is held from now (back to you if they decline or you call it off).
  2. They accept: their stake is held too, until it's settled.
  3. Each of you plays the 9 holes on your own PC, whenever you like, within 7 days. Same course, same wind, same greens for both. Your friend's card stays hidden until yours is in.
  4. When both cards are in the bet settles by itself (handicap strokes come off the scores first): the winner gets the pot, and you both see the shared scorecard.
  5. Not played in time? Whoever didn't play loses by forfeit; if neither of you played, both stakes come back.
How an invitational works — the same as a challenge, for as many friends as you like:
  1. Pick your friends and send it. Your stake is held from now.
  2. Each friend accepts or declines. A friend's stake is held when they accept.
  3. You start it once at least one friend is in. Anyone who hasn't accepted by then is left out and pays nothing.
  4. Everyone plays the 9 holes on their own PC within 7 days: same course, wind and greens for all.
  5. When every card is in it settles. Stroke play: the lowest net total takes the whole pot (a tie splits it). Skins: each hole is worth the stake from everyone, won by the one lowest score; a tie carries.
